title: Ontop (SQL Bridge)

narrative_arc.enters_knowing: They have a SQL database and want to expose it as SPARQL without ETL.
narrative_arc.leaves_knowing: What Ontop is, that it is an external tool (not Mat-O-Lab maintained), when to use it, and how its virtual SPARQL output can connect to the DataStack.
steps: What Ontop is — OBDA (Ontology-Based Data Access) bridge, virtual SPARQL over SQL, no ETL
External tool note — not maintained by Mat-O-Lab; link to Ontop documentation
R2RML/OBDA mapping — minimal explanation, link to Ontop docs
Integration with DataStack — Ontop SPARQL endpoint can serve as data source for downstream mapping
No Mat-O-Lab integration built yet — honest limitation

quality_gate: Kept short — no more than one page of content
notes: Lowest priority. Keep short — explain what it is, link to official docs, note the gap. No Mat-O-Lab-specific content exists. If no meaningful content can be added beyond the stub, keep with '!!! info "External tool"' admonition and links.

primary.name: Domain Scientist
knows: Their scientific domain deeply (materials science, microscopy, lab procedures)
Measurement concepts and experimental workflows they consider universal
Domain-specific tools (OMERO, ELN systems, instrument software)
does_not_know: Ontology terms like PMDCO, CHAMEO, EMMO even if these describe their own work
How ontologies model domain concepts — that this modeling discipline exists at all
SPARQL, RDF, or any semantic technology
primary.goal: Upload their data, trigger the pipeline, and use or export FAIR-compliant results.
primary.key_gap: Double gap: (1) no semantic web knowledge whatsoever, and (2) domain experts frequently assume their concepts are universal common knowledge when they are not — documentation must not assume shared domain vocabulary and must explain what gets modeled and why, not just how.
